speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I see you present with gait and limb ataxia; to begin our investigation, please describe when these symptoms first started and if they are worsening over time. Additionally, you mentioned a significant medical history—what specific conditions have you been diagnosed with in the past?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: The patient describes recent onset of gait and limb ataxia, noting a "drunk" appearance and clumsiness specifically on the right side. Regarding your significant medical history you mentioned, could you please list the specific conditions you have been diagnosed with in the past?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: PML (Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy) induced by natalizumab.

Given your history of Crohn's disease and natalizumab use, the new onset of unilateral ataxia is highly suspicious for an opportunistic infection like PML. Have you experienced any visual changes, weakness, or cognitive difficulties alongside the clumsiness? REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Brain.
